before_strategy: (1) For each $n \in \mathbb{N}$ define $\varphi_n : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} \setminus \{n\}$ by $\varphi_n(k) = k$ for $k < n$ and $\varphi_n(k) = \sigma(k)$ for $k \ge n$. Trichotomy makes it a function; $\sigma$ injective and $\sigma(k) > k$ make it injective; and it is onto: for $m < n$ take $k = m$, and for $m > n$ write $m = \sigma(j)$ ([[lem-nat-nonzero-is-successor]]) with $n \le j$ by discreteness ([[lem-nat-discrete]]), so $\varphi_n(j) = m$. (2) For countably infinite $X$ fix a bijection $e : \mathbb{N} \to X$ and $x = e(n)$; then $e \circ \varphi_n \circ e^{-1}$ is a bijection $X \to X$ with image $e[\mathbb{N} \setminus \{n\}] = X \setminus \{x\}$, the image computed from injectivity of $e$. (3) Contrast: if a finite $F$ had a proper subset $A$ with $F \approx A$, transporting along a bijection $F \to m$ would give $m \approx \varphi^{-1}[A]$ with $\varphi^{-1}[A]$ a proper subset of $m$, contradicting claim 5 of [[lem-pigeonhole]].

Trichotomy makes it a function; $\sigma$ injective and $\sigma(k) > k$ make it injective; and it is onto: for $m < n$ take $k = m$, and for $m > n$ write $m = \sigma(j)$ ([[lem-nat-nonzero-is-successor]]) with $n \le j$ by discreteness ([[lem-nat-discrete]]), so $\varphi_n(j) = m$. (2) For countably infinite $X$ fix a bijection $e : \mathbb{N} \to X$ and $x = e(n)$; then $e \circ \varphi_n \circ e^{-1}$ is a bijection from $X$ onto $X \setminus \{x\}$, whose image is $e[\mathbb{N} \setminus \{n\}] = X \setminus \{x\}$, the image computed from injectivity of $e$. formal_statement_unchanged: Let $X$ be countably infinite ([[def-countable]]) and let $x \in X$. Then $X \approx X \setminus \{x\}$ ([[def-equinumerous]]): deleting one point leaves a set of the same size, and $X \setminus \{x\}$ is a proper subset of $X$ ([[def-set-difference-and-symmetric-difference]], [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]). The basic instance is $X = \mathbb{N}$, $x = 0$, where the witness is the successor map $\sigma$, a bijection $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} \setminus \{0\}$ ([[thm-omega-is-peano-system]], [[lem-nat-nonzero-is-successor]]); a general $X$ transports a shift of $\mathbb{N}$ along a bijection $\mathbb{N} \to X$ ([[thm-a-function-is-a-bijection-exactly-when-it-has-a-two-sided-inverse]], [[prop-composition-preserves-injectivity-surjectivity-and-bijectivity]]). No finite set shares the behaviour: by claim 5 of [[lem-pigeonhole]] no finite set is equinumerous with a proper subset of itself. No choice principle is used.
